## Observed

pm-jev#99 went red after a single `pm comment` on one of its in-progress items. No code changed. CI ran `changelog:check`, which refused the committed CHANGELOG.md: the only difference was the position of that item's line within `### Fixed` ([job 127733701630](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/actions/runs/42169494017/job/127733701630)).

## Cause

`compareItems` (`src/generator.ts`, around line 2589) orders entries by `itemTimestamp()`, newest first. For an item with no `completed_at` or `closed_at`, that resolves to `updated_at`.

The fleet's changelog scripts pass `--status closed,in_progress`, so every in-progress item in a PR window is ordered by its last metadata write. That write can be a comment, a linked file, a test run or a claim. Any of them reorders the section, and `changelog:check` fails until someone regenerates and commits again.

This is the class #6 fixed for version sections, now inside one section. It costs a CI round every time an agent or orchestrator documents its work, which the fleet requires.

## Expected

The order within a section does not change when pm metadata that is not a lifecycle field changes. For example:

- Closed items sort by completion timestamp, as now.
- Items without a completion timestamp sort by a stable key (`created_at`, then `id`), never by `updated_at`.

Add a regression test: a comment on an in-progress item leaves the generated changelog byte-identical.

## Workaround in the fleet today

Rerun `npm run changelog:full` and commit after every pm write on an open PR.
Section order follows updated_at for in-progress items, so any pm comment fails changelog:check
